# Requirements Document ## Introduction The project-showcase spec delivers a `/projects` gallery and per-project detail pages at `/projects/[slug]`, driven by a new Velite `projects` collection of MDX files in `content/projects/`. Each project entry carries structured frontmatter (title, description, summary, date, cover image, tags, status, and a `links` map for live demos, repositories, etc.) plus an MDX body for the long-form writeup, screenshots, and embedded media. The gallery presents reverse-chronological visual cards keyed on the cover image; clicking through navigates to a per-project page with the rendered MDX body and a link rail. After this spec ships, Matthew can add a project by dropping `content/projects/.mdx` plus colocated images, committing, and letting CI redeploy — the gallery card and detail page appear with no React changes. Search indexing (Pagefind), cross-linking from blog posts to project pages, the landing-page hero-card preview of recent projects, and any contributions-gallery / resources surfaces are explicitly out of scope and belong to later specs (contributions-and-resources, slash-pages, or future polish work). Project filtering by tag is out of scope at launch — projects are expected to number in the single digits for the foreseeable future and a flat reverse-chronological list is sufficient. Tag display on cards/detail pages is in scope; tag *navigation* (clickable, filtered indexes) is not. ## Alignment with Product Vision - **Builder credibility** (product.md business objective #2): The project gallery is the primary surface where visitors see what Matthew has built — a working showcase materially supports the "active building" signal the site sells. - **Markdown-first content** (product principle #2): Project entries live as `.mdx` files with frontmatter. The React layer renders structure (cards, headers, link rails, image grids); it never owns prose or screenshot lists. - **Simple to maintain** (product principle #3): Adding a project is `content/projects/.mdx` + image assets + commit. Schema validation, slug derivation, sitemap inclusion, and image processing all happen at build time. - **Wide and spacious** (product principle #1): Project detail pages may include wide imagery (screenshots, GIF captures). The detail layout uses a wider content container than the blog post column, while constraining body prose to the ~75-character measure for readability. - **Responsive** (product principle #6): Gallery cards reflow from a multi-column grid on desktop to a single column on mobile. Cover images use responsive `sizes` and Next.js Image optimization. - **Accessible** (product principle #7): Cover images carry author-supplied alt text (a schema-required field, not derived). Cards are keyboard-navigable as a single link target per card. Color contrast and focus states meet WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes. - **Performance** (product success metric #4): Both the gallery and detail pages are statically generated. Images are optimized to WebP/AVIF by Next.js Image. No client-side filtering, sorting, or hydration is required to read a project. - **Independence from platforms** (business objective #4): The gallery is hosted on `matthewfield.ca`; external project links are presented in a link rail but the source-of-truth narrative lives on the personal site. ## Requirements ### Requirement 1: `projects` Velite collection and content directory **User Story:** As Matthew, I want to add a project by dropping an MDX file (plus images) into `content/projects/` and committing, so that I never edit React code to launch or update a project entry. The publishing workflow is `git commit && git push && wait for CI`; a successful Vercel build/deploy is a publishing prerequisite. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The Velite configuration (`velite.config.ts`) SHALL define a new top-level collection named `projects` with `pattern: "projects/*.mdx"` (flat — slugs are single-segment, no nested project directories). The collection SHALL be registered in `defineConfig({ collections })` alongside the existing `pages`, `profile`, and `posts` collections. The existing collections SHALL remain unchanged. 2. The `projects` schema SHALL require the following frontmatter fields: - `title` (string, 1–120 characters — used as the gallery card heading, the detail page `

`, and the `` element via the site-wide title template). - `description` (string, 1–300 characters — used as the meta description AND, by default, the gallery-card body copy; see Req 2.4 for the override mechanism). - `date` (ISO 8601 datetime — the project's publication date for the gallery's reverse-chronological order; for ongoing projects this is the date Matthew first published the writeup, not a "start date"). - `cover` (Velite `s.image()` — relative path to a colocated cover image; Velite resolves and copies it to the built asset output. The schema SHALL reject missing files. See Req 3 for image semantics). - `coverAlt` (string, 1–250 characters — alt text for the cover image. This is REQUIRED, not optional; an image without alt text is an accessibility failure and the build SHALL refuse to ship one. The schema-level requirement closes the "author forgot alt text" failure mode at build time, not at review time). - `tags` (array of strings, 0–8 entries; each enforced against the kebab-slug regex `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` matching the posts-collection convention from blog-core. Empty array is acceptable — tags are author-organizational, not navigational at launch). - `status` (string enum — one of `active`, `archived`, `concept`; default `active`. See Req 4 for the display semantics. Status is information *for the reader*, not a list-filter). 3. The `projects` schema SHALL support the following optional frontmatter fields: - `summary` (string, 1–300 characters — gallery-card body copy override. When absent, the gallery card SHALL use `description` per Req 2.4. The split exists so the meta-description text can be SEO-tuned without forcing a poor gallery card, and vice versa). - `updated` (ISO 8601 datetime — author-controlled "meaningful content update" marker, mirroring the posts-collection convention. The schema SHALL NOT derive `updated` from git history — see Req 1.5 below for the rationale). - `draft` (boolean, default `false` — see Req 7 for production exclusion semantics, which mirror the posts-collection draft contract). - `slug` (string override — when present, used verbatim as the route segment, must match the kebab-slug regex from Req 1.2; when absent, derived from the filename per Req 1.4). - `featured` (boolean, default `false` — opt-in marker for the per-card visual treatment in Req 2.7. Not a sort-key — featured projects are not floated to the top of the gallery; chronological order is preserved). - `links` (object, optional — keyed map of named external links. See Req 5 for the schema, validation, and rendering rules). - `body` (transformed via `s.mdx()` — required field implicitly populated by Velite from the file body, not authored as frontmatter). 4. WHEN a project file is `content/projects/<filename>.mdx` AND no explicit `slug` frontmatter is set THEN the route segment SHALL equal `<filename>` (without the `.mdx` extension), and the Velite-emitted `slug` field on the parsed project SHALL match. The schema SHALL apply Velite's `s.path()` primitive followed by a `.transform()` that strips the leading `projects/` prefix — matching the pattern already established for `pages` at `velite.config.ts` and for `posts` in the blog-core implementation. 5. **Author-controlled `updated` (deliberate divergence from `profile`, parity with `posts`)**: The `projects` schema SHALL NOT derive `updated` from git history. The `profile` collection uses `git log -1 --format=%cI` because the file IS the resume and every commit is a content update. A project's git history accumulates typo fixes, broken-link patches, screenshot swaps, and frontmatter tweaks; automated derivation would surface every such commit as a misleading "Updated on …" badge. Authors SHALL explicitly set `updated` in frontmatter when (and only when) the change is meaningful to readers. Absent `updated` means "no meaningful update since publication." 6. WHEN the build runs AND a project file violates the schema (missing required field, invalid datetime, invalid string length, unknown frontmatter key with `.strict()` in effect, invalid `status` enum value, invalid tag slug, missing or invalid cover image) THEN the Velite build SHALL fail with a named error identifying the offending file and field. The build SHALL NOT silently coerce, default-fill, or skip the malformed project. 7. The `projects` schema SHALL use `.strict()` mode so a typo like `coverr:` or `tagz:` is a build-time error rather than a silent omission. 8. WHEN `content/projects/` is empty (zero MDX files) THEN the Velite build SHALL succeed and emit `projects: []`. The same downstream code paths (Req 2 gallery, Req 6 detail-page static params, sitemap inclusion) SHALL all handle an empty `projects` array without erroring. This mirrors the empty-collection contract that blog-core and site-foundation already enforce. 9. The Velite output type for a `projects` entry — exposed via the `#site/content` path alias — SHALL include both the raw frontmatter fields AND the computed fields (`slug`, transformed `cover` with resolved asset path + width/height/blurDataURL where `s.image()` provides them, `body` MDX code). Downstream importers (`src/lib/projects.ts`, page components) SHALL consume the typed collection; ad-hoc `JSON.parse` of `.velite/projects.json` is prohibited. 10. **Order-of-operations for landing the schema and content**: Implementation SHALL land the new Velite `projects` collection schema (in `velite.config.ts`), the initial content directory `content/projects/` with at least one `placeholder.mdx` (marked `draft: true` so it doesn't ship), and the route files for `/projects` and `/projects/[slug]` in the SAME commit (or in a sequence where each intermediate commit leaves CI green). Splitting them creates windows where either Velite fails (collection registered, directory missing) or the route files reference an unregistered collection. ### Requirement 2: Gallery page at `/projects` **User Story:** As a visitor, I want to land on `/projects` and see a visual gallery of Matthew's projects, so that I can quickly scan what he has built and click through to whatever catches my eye. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/projects` THEN the page SHALL render a reverse-chronological grid of project cards, sorted by `date` descending (newest first), with `slug` ascending as the tiebreak for same-day entries. This sort SHALL be implemented as a single shared comparator in `src/lib/projects.ts` (mirroring the `byDateDescSlugAsc` pattern in `src/lib/blog.ts`) so the gallery, sitemap inclusion, and any future surfaces use one source of truth. 2. WHEN the gallery is rendered THEN it SHALL be a statically generated server component. To prevent silent degradation to dynamic rendering, `/projects/page.tsx` AND `/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` SHALL declare `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. 3. WHEN the gallery is rendered THEN each project card SHALL include, in DOM order: - The cover image (Req 3) rendered via the Next.js `<Image>` component, including the author-supplied `coverAlt`. - The project title. - The project body copy (per Req 2.4). - The publication date (`date` field, formatted via the same Intl `DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { year, month, day })` formatter the blog uses for parity). - Tags as plain (non-interactive) text labels — see Req 2.5. - A "status badge" iff `status !== "active"` — see Req 4. - The card itself wrapped in a single anchor element (`<a href="/projects/[slug]">`) covering the entire card surface, with the title as the accessible link name; the image carries empty `alt=""` if the same card surface also surfaces the title text within the link (per Req 2.6's exact link-text contract). 4. The card body copy SHALL be `project.summary` when present, falling back to `project.description` otherwise. This split exists so the meta-description text can be SEO-tuned without forcing a poor gallery card, and a project author can write a punchier card line without diluting the SEO field. 5. Tag display on cards SHALL render each tag as a non-interactive `<span>` (NOT a link). At launch, tags are author-organizational metadata, not a navigation surface. This requirement explicitly forecloses adding `/projects/tag/[tag]` taxonomy routes in this spec. 6. **Card link semantics — explicit "one link per card" contract**: Each project card SHALL be a SINGLE anchor element wrapping the entire card surface. The card SHALL NOT nest a "Read more" link, a separate title link, or any other secondary anchor inside the same card. The card SHALL NOT render the `links` rail (Req 5) — those are exclusively a detail-page concern. The single-link-per-card rule is non-negotiable because nested anchors are invalid HTML and screen readers announce each card as a single, predictable list item. 7. **Featured-card variant**: WHEN a card's underlying project has `featured: true` THEN the card MAY render with a visually emphasized treatment (e.g. larger grid span, accent border). The exact visual treatment is a design-phase concern; this requirement guarantees only that (a) the data plumbing for the `featured` flag reaches the card component, (b) the sort order is NOT altered (Req 2.1 stands — `featured` is a presentation hint, not a sort key), and (c) the card's link semantics (Req 2.6) are unchanged. 8. WHEN the gallery page is rendered THEN its `<title>` SHALL be "Projects" composed through the site-wide `%s | matthewfield.ca` title template, and its meta description SHALL be a short author-curated string defined in the page component (NOT pulled from MDX, since the gallery is not MDX-driven). The OG image MAY be the site default per the metadata convention site-foundation established. 9. WHEN no projects are published (production build with `projects: []` after `draft` filtering) THEN the gallery page SHALL render a copy block stating "No projects published yet." The page SHALL NOT throw, return a blank page, or 404. The block MAY include a one-line "Check back later" line. Detail-route static params for `/projects/[slug]` SHALL be `[]` in this case — Next.js's `generateStaticParams` accepts an empty array without error. 10. WHEN the gallery is viewed on a narrow viewport (<640px) THEN cards SHALL stack in a single column. Exact breakpoints, gutter sizing, and column counts at intermediate widths are design-phase concerns; this requirement guarantees only that mobile renders one card per row, not that the page horizontally scrolls or that cards overflow. ### Requirement 3: Cover image handling **User Story:** As Matthew, I want to drop a project's cover image next to its MDX file and have it processed, optimized, and rendered correctly, so that the gallery and detail page look polished without me running an image pipeline by hand. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The `cover` frontmatter field SHALL be typed as Velite's `s.image()` primitive with a relative path value (e.g. `./cover.png` or `./screenshots/cover.png`). Velite SHALL resolve the path against the project file's own directory, copy the asset to the built output at `public/static/`, and emit a transformed value containing the deployed URL plus image metadata (`width`, `height`, optionally a `blurDataURL` if Velite's pipeline produces one). 2. WHEN the cover-image file is missing or unreadable at build time THEN the Velite build SHALL fail with a named error identifying the offending project file and the missing image path. The build SHALL NOT emit a placeholder, leave `cover` as `undefined`, or skip the project. 3. Content images for a project (cover image + any in-body images referenced from the MDX) SHALL be colocated under `content/projects/` and addressed by relative path. **Permitted layouts** (either works, picked per project): - **Flat-with-sibling-assets**: `content/projects/foo.mdx` plus `content/projects/foo-cover.png`, `content/projects/foo-screenshot-1.png`, … (the cover frontmatter references `./foo-cover.png`). This works because each project's image filenames carry the slug as a prefix, avoiding collisions between sibling projects. - **Per-project subdirectory**: `content/projects/foo.mdx` plus `content/projects/foo/cover.png`, `content/projects/foo/screenshot-1.png`, … (the cover frontmatter references `./foo/cover.png`). This works because the Velite glob `projects/*.mdx` is flat — the subdirectory holds assets only, not other MDX files. - The build pipeline (Velite's `s.image()` resolver + the `content/projects/`-relative copy-to-`public/static/` step) SHALL work for BOTH layouts without per-project configuration. 4. WHEN a project's cover image is rendered on the gallery card THEN it SHALL use the Next.js `<Image>` component with the resolved URL, the schema's `width`/`height` for layout stability (preventing Cumulative Layout Shift), and a `sizes` attribute appropriate for the gallery grid breakpoints. The exact `sizes` value is a design-phase concern; this requirement guarantees only that `sizes` is set and that intrinsic dimensions come from Velite metadata, not hard-coded in the component. 5. WHEN a project's cover image is rendered on the detail page (`/projects/[slug]`) THEN it SHALL likewise use the Next.js `<Image>` component with the resolved URL and Velite-supplied dimensions. The detail-page rendering MAY use a larger `sizes` value than the card (since the detail layout gives the cover more real estate). The author's `coverAlt` is reused. 6. Cover images SHALL be served from the same domain as the site (`/static/...`), not from a third-party host. This is a consequence of Velite's standard behavior (copy assets into the Next.js public directory) and is restated here because it has a CSP and privacy implication: `img-src 'self' data:` from the site-foundation CSP suffices, no external image source needs to be added. 7. In-body images (referenced via standard MDX/Markdown image syntax inside the MDX `body`) SHALL flow through the same MDX rehype pipeline the rest of the site uses. The site SHALL NOT add a project-specific image transform that rewrites the user's MDX. If the existing pipeline does NOT auto-wrap markdown images with `next/image`, then in-body images render as plain `<img>` and are not optimized — this is acceptable for launch (cover image carries the visual weight; in-body images are screenshot supplements that authors can size sensibly). Adding MDX-image optimization is a future-spec enhancement and is explicitly out of scope here. 8. **No upper bound on cover-image dimensions is enforced at the schema level** at launch. Authors are trusted to provide reasonably sized cover images (Next.js Image handles the responsive resize, but the source still ships through Velite). If a multi-megabyte cover image lands and degrades build time or first paint, the remediation is "shrink the source," not a runtime cap. A future enhancement can add a build-time warning for cover images above some size threshold; not in this spec. ### Requirement 4: Project status display **User Story:** As a visitor, I want to see at a glance whether a project is still being worked on, archived, or just a concept, so that I can calibrate my expectations before clicking through. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The `status` field SHALL be one of the literal strings `active`, `archived`, or `concept`. Schema validation SHALL enforce the enum via `s.enum(["active", "archived", "concept"])` (or equivalent) and reject any other string with a build-time error per Req 1.6. 2. WHEN a project's `status === "active"` (the default) THEN the gallery card and detail page SHALL NOT render any status badge. "Active" is the unmarked baseline — the absence of a badge IS the active signal. This minimizes visual noise. 3. WHEN a project's `status === "archived"` THEN both the gallery card AND the detail page SHALL render a textual status badge with the visible label "Archived." The badge SHALL be a non-interactive element (no link, no tooltip required), positioned so a sighted viewer cannot mistake the project for one in active development. 4. WHEN a project's `status === "concept"` THEN both the gallery card AND the detail page SHALL render a textual status badge with the visible label "Concept." The exact visual treatment is a design-phase concern; the requirement guarantees that the badge is visually distinguishable from the "Archived" badge so the reader does not have to compare to other projects to decode which state the marker indicates. 5. Status badges SHALL be plain rendered text in the static HTML (no client-side JS required to display them). They SHALL be screen-reader accessible (e.g. `<span>Archived</span>` is sufficient; no decorative-icon-only badges). 6. Status SHALL NOT change the gallery sort order or hide a project from the gallery. An archived project still appears in `/projects` chronologically alongside active and concept projects, distinguished only by the badge. This keeps the gallery comprehensible as a complete record of work, not a curated filter view. ### Requirement 5: External links rail on the detail page **User Story:** As a visitor reading a project detail page, I want to find the live demo, the source repository, and any other relevant external links in one predictable place, so that I don't have to scan the prose for "where do I click to try this." #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The `links` frontmatter field, when present, SHALL be an object whose keys are link-purpose identifiers and whose values are URL strings. Permitted keys at launch: - `demo` — a live demo or hosted application URL. - `repo` — a public source-code repository URL (typically GitHub). - `docs` — published documentation, a tech writeup, or a deeper teardown that lives off-site. - `package` — a published package on a registry (e.g. npm, crates.io, PyPI). - `writeup` — a related blog post or external article (when the project page itself is short). 2. Each value in the `links` object SHALL be validated as a URL via Velite's `s.string().url()` primitive (or equivalent). The schema SHALL use `.strict()` so unknown keys (e.g. `dem0:`) cause a build-time error rather than silently dropping the link. Each URL SHALL use `http://` or `https://` — `mailto:`, `tel:`, `javascript:`, and `data:` schemes SHALL be rejected. (Validation: explicit regex/protocol check after `s.string().url()`, since `url()` accepts `mailto:` and `javascript:` URLs by default.) 3. WHEN the `links` object is absent or `{}` THEN the link rail SHALL NOT be rendered on the detail page. There SHALL NOT be an empty container, a "No links yet" placeholder, or a disabled-looking shell. 4. WHEN the link rail is rendered THEN it SHALL appear ABOVE the MDX body on the detail page, in a position the visitor sees before scrolling into prose. Each link SHALL render with a fixed visible label per key (`Live demo`, `Repository`, `Docs`, `Package`, `Writeup`) — the *visible* label is fixed regardless of the URL contents. Visible labels for additional keys MAY be added in future enhancements; the launch set is the five keys in Req 5.1. 5. Each link in the rail SHALL open in the same tab by default (no `target="_blank"`) and SHALL carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"` regardless of `target` — `noopener` is meaningful even for same-tab clicks initiated from a different origin context, and `noreferrer` is a privacy default for outbound links from a personal site. Authors are not given a per-link override; a uniform policy is simpler than a per-link toggle. 6. The link rail SHALL appear ONLY on the detail page, NOT on the gallery card. Per Req 2.6, each card has exactly one link target (the detail page). Surfacing the rail on the card would violate the single-anchor-per-card contract and is forbidden. 7. The link rail SHALL be a server-rendered region (no client-side JS required). Each link SHALL be a plain `<a>` element. Icons MAY be added in the design phase but the visible text label SHALL remain present for screen readers — the rail SHALL NOT degrade to icon-only. ### Requirement 6: Detail page at `/projects/[slug]` **User Story:** As a visitor, I want to click a card and land on a page with the full project writeup — the story, screenshots, technical details — so that I can dig in beyond the gallery summary. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/projects/<slug>` for a published project (not `draft`) THEN the page SHALL render with, in DOM order: the project title (`<h1>`), the publication date, the status badge (when applicable, per Req 4), the cover image, the link rail (per Req 5, when applicable), and the MDX body content. 2. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/projects/<slug>` for a slug that does NOT correspond to a published project (file does not exist, slug typo, draft in production, or `[slug]` collision) THEN the page SHALL return a 404 via Next.js's `notFound()` API, not a blank page, not a runtime SSR error. 3. WHEN a project's `updated` frontmatter is present AND is strictly later than `date` THEN the detail page SHALL display an "Updated on <date>" badge near the publication date. The badge SHALL use the same Intl `DateTimeFormat("en-CA")` formatter as `date`. The shared helper SHALL live in `src/lib/projects.ts` (e.g. `shouldShowUpdatedBadge(project)` and `formatProjectDate(iso)` — mirroring the blog-core helpers) so the same predicate is used on both the gallery card and detail page. 4. The detail page's `<title>` SHALL be `project.title` composed through the site-wide `%s | matthewfield.ca` template. The meta description SHALL be `project.description`. The OG image SHALL be the resolved cover image URL — projects are inherently visual, the cover is the canonical share image. 5. The detail page SHALL be a statically generated server component. `/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` SHALL implement `generateStaticParams()` returning the list of published-project slugs (drafts excluded in production, see Req 7). It SHALL declare `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` to forbid silent degradation to dynamic rendering. 6. WHEN the MDX body uses h2 or h3 headings THEN each SHALL render with an anchor ID (via `rehype-slug`, already in the shared rehype pipeline) so that `/projects/<slug>#some-heading` deep links work. The detail page SHALL NOT render a separate table-of-contents component at launch — project pages are expected to be shorter than blog posts and a TOC is overkill. A future enhancement may add one. 7. The detail page's content container width SHALL be the same `max-w-5xl` (1024 px / 64 rem) Tailwind utility the `/profile` page uses — wider than the blog's prose column to accommodate screenshots, but narrower than full-bleed. Prose body inside that container SHALL still respect the ~75-character measure (product principle #1) via standard Tailwind prose typography utilities. 8. WHEN the build runs THEN it SHALL fail loudly on ANY of the following conditions: (a) frontmatter schema violations (Velite), (b) MDX compile errors in a project body, (c) references to undefined MDX components, (d) render-time exceptions during static generation of `/projects/[slug]`. No error class SHALL degrade to runtime SSR, a blank page, or a silent omission of the project from the gallery. 9. The project MDX body has NO custom component registry at launch. The existing `<MDXContent />` component renders MDX via `new Function(code)(runtime)` with no `components` argument, so capitalized-tag references (e.g. `<Screenshot />`, `<Demo />`) WOULD produce a `ReferenceError` at static-generation time — Req 6.8(c)/(d) then surfaces this as a build failure, correctly. Authors SHALL write project bodies as plain-markdown-equivalent MDX with no custom component tags. Future specs MAY add a registry; this one does not. 10. The detail page SHALL NOT render previous/next-project navigation at launch. Project pages are intentionally "landing pages" for each project; the gallery is the index. (Blog posts have prev/next because readers walk a chronological column; project visitors are looking for a specific project, not browsing chronologically.) A future enhancement may revisit this. 11. The detail page SHALL NOT render related-project suggestions, comments, or social-share buttons at launch. All explicitly deferred. 12. The detail page SHALL render the `coverAlt` author-supplied alt text on the detail-page cover image. (Cards may render the cover with empty `alt=""` per Req 2.3's link-name contract; the detail page is the surface where the alt text is non-redundant and SHALL carry it.) ### Requirement 7: Draft handling and production exclusion **User Story:** As Matthew, I want to write a project entry while still polishing it without it leaking into the public site, so that I can iterate locally and on PR previews without committing to publish. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The `draft` field defaults to `false`. WHEN `draft === true` AND the build is the production deploy THEN the project SHALL be excluded from `getPublishedProjects()` (the central query helper), and therefore SHALL NOT appear in the gallery, in `generateStaticParams()` for `/projects/[slug]`, in the XML sitemap, in any future related-project rails, or anywhere else a published-projects list is consumed. 2. WHEN `draft === true` AND the build is local (no `VERCEL` env var) THEN the project SHALL be included in the gallery and reachable at `/projects/<slug>` ONLY when `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` is set in the environment. The toggle is opt-in. Without it, drafts are excluded locally too — local builds default to production-equivalent behavior so a draft does not unexpectedly appear when running `pnpm dev`. 3. WHEN `draft === true` AND the build is a Vercel preview deploy (`VERCEL_ENV === "preview"`) THEN behavior SHALL follow the same layered draft-leak-guard pattern blog-core established in `src/lib/blog-errors.ts`: if the production-vs-preview environment scoping is misconfigured such that production code paths would include drafts, the helper SHALL throw a named error from `src/lib/project-errors.ts` (paralleling `BLOG_DRAFT_LEAK_GUARD_MSG_PRODUCTION` / `BLOG_DRAFT_LEAK_GUARD_MSG_PREVIEW`) so a real production deploy fails fast instead of leaking drafts. 4. `src/lib/projects.ts` SHALL expose a `getPublishedProjects(): Project[]` helper that applies the draft filter (per Req 7.1–7.3) and returns a stable, sorted list (per Req 2.1). All consumer surfaces — the gallery page, the detail page's `generateStaticParams()`, sitemap inclusion, any future surfaces — SHALL call this helper rather than importing `projects` from `#site/content` directly. Direct imports of the raw collection bypass the draft filter and the leak guard, and are prohibited in the consuming app code. 5. WHEN a draft project is published (i.e. `draft: true` is removed or set to `false`) AND CI runs THEN the project's first public appearance SHALL include all of: gallery card, detail page, sitemap entry. There SHALL NOT be a separate "publish" action — flipping the frontmatter and committing IS the publish. 6. **Tests for the draft-leak guard SHALL be written**: A unit test in `src/lib/projects.test.ts` SHALL verify (a) that `getPublishedProjects()` excludes drafts when `VERCEL_ENV=production`, (b) that the production guard throws when the leak-guard precondition fires, and (c) that `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` includes drafts only when no `VERCEL` env var is set. The pattern mirrors `src/lib/blog.test.ts` from blog-core. ### Requirement 8: Sitemap and discoverability **User Story:** As a visitor or search engine, I want every published project to appear in the site's XML sitemap, so that nothing is hidden from discovery. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. WHEN the site's XML sitemap (existing at `/sitemap.xml`, generated by `src/app/sitemap.ts` per site-foundation) is built THEN it SHALL include one entry per published project, with `url: <siteUrl>/projects/<slug>` and `lastModified` set to `project.updated ?? project.date`. 2. The sitemap entry for the gallery itself (`/projects`) SHALL exist regardless of whether any projects are published — the page itself is a stable URL, even when its body says "No projects published yet." 3. Drafts SHALL NEVER appear in the sitemap, in any environment. (Local builds with `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` set MAY include them — the toggle is local-dev-only and the sitemap consumed by search engines is the production build's.) 4. The sitemap implementation SHALL consume `getPublishedProjects()` per Req 7.4 — it SHALL NOT re-implement the draft filter or re-import the raw Velite collection. 5. The XML sitemap SHALL NOT add a separate sub-sitemap (e.g. `/projects-sitemap.xml`). Project URLs join the existing single sitemap. Splitting is a scale optimization (>50k URLs) and irrelevant at this site's size. ### Requirement 9: Non-Functional Requirements #### Code Architecture and Modularity - **Single Responsibility Principle**: `src/lib/projects.ts` owns query helpers (sort, filter, formatters, leak guards). The gallery card component owns card layout. The detail page owns detail layout. No business logic in page files beyond data wiring. - **Modular Design**: The gallery card component SHALL be usable from any future surface (e.g. a "recent projects" rail on the landing page) without modification. It accepts a typed `Project` and renders independently. - **Pattern reuse over abstraction**: The project query helpers parallel the blog query helpers (`getPublishedPosts`, `shouldShowUpdatedBadge`, `byDateDescSlugAsc`, `formatPostDate`). Authors SHALL NOT extract a shared "content collection" base class at this point — three collections (`posts`, `projects`, future `contributions`) is too small a population to amortize the abstraction cost. Each helper module remains independent and concrete. - **Clear Interfaces**: `Project` type derived from the Velite collection. All public functions in `src/lib/projects.ts` return `Project` or simple primitive shapes (string, boolean, sorted array). - **No direct collection imports outside `src/lib/projects.ts`**: Page components, the sitemap, and any future consumers SHALL go through the helpers. This is enforced by code review at launch; a future ESLint rule could mechanize it. #### Performance - **Static generation**: Both `/projects` (gallery) and `/projects/[slug]` (detail) are statically generated at build time. No per-request rendering, no client-side data fetching. - **Image optimization**: Cover images flow through Next.js Image (WebP/AVIF, responsive `sizes`, lazy-loading off-screen). In-body MDX images are not auto-optimized (per Req 3.7); authors are expected to provide reasonably sized assets. - **Lighthouse target**: Gallery and detail pages SHALL meet the site's 90+ Lighthouse performance score (product.md Performance constraint), measured on a representative build. Baseline JS overhead is the Next.js floor (~60-85KB per page) per tech.md's known limitation; no project-specific client JS is added. - **Bundle impact**: This spec SHALL NOT add new client-side JavaScript libraries. The gallery and detail pages are entirely server-rendered. Any new packages (e.g. for image processing) SHALL be build-time-only — checked at PR review. #### Security - **CSP unchanged**: `/projects` and `/projects/[slug]` are content pages under the site-foundation CSP. Cover images are first-party (`/static/...`), so `img-src 'self' data:` continues to suffice — no CSP changes are required. - **External link safety**: All links in the detail-page rail (Req 5) SHALL carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. URL validation SHALL reject `javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, and `tel:` schemes at the schema layer (Req 5.2). - **MDX content**: Project MDX bodies execute through the same MDX compilation pipeline as the rest of the site; there is no per-spec security surface beyond what blog-core and professional-profile already address. Authors are trusted (Matthew is the only author). - **No user input on these pages**: Neither page accepts form input. The contact form (professional-profile) is the only user-input surface and is not reused here. #### Reliability - **Build-time validation everywhere**: Schema violations, missing cover images, invalid URL schemes, and broken MDX SHALL all fail the build with a named error per Req 1.6, 3.2, 5.2, and 6.8. The build SHALL NOT degrade silently. - **Empty-collection contract**: A site with zero projects SHALL build, deploy, and serve `/projects` with a "No projects yet" message. The detail-page route SHALL produce zero static params and SHALL NOT error. - **Internal-link integrity**: Internal links pointing into the project subtree (e.g. `/projects/foo`) SHALL be exercised by the existing CI link checker (per tech.md), with internal-link failures blocking the deploy. External links in the rail are subject to the same warning-only policy as elsewhere on the site. - **Draft-leak guard**: Layered guards in `src/lib/project-errors.ts` SHALL fail the production build (or production-equivalent code path) if draft inclusion is somehow about to leak — mirroring the blog-core leak-guard architecture. Unit tests SHALL exercise the guard. #### Usability - **Single-anchor cards**: Each gallery card is one click target with a predictable accessible name (Req 2.6). No nested anchors, no "Read more" duplicates. - **Status communicated visually AND textually**: Archived and Concept badges (Req 4) are plain text, never icon-only. - **Predictable navigation**: Gallery → click a card → land on the project page → click an external link in the rail → land on demo/repo. There SHALL be no surprise modals, no "Are you sure?" interstitials, no JS-driven transitions that interrupt browser back-navigation. - **Theme parity**: Both gallery and detail pages SHALL look correct in light AND dark mode. Cover images are author-provided assets, so light/dark theme switching does NOT swap a separate light/dark cover; authors who want a light-or-dark-specific cover SHALL pick one that reads in both themes. (Per-theme cover variants are a future enhancement and not in scope.) - **Mobile rendering**: Both pages SHALL render and scroll cleanly at mobile viewport widths (≤640 px) without horizontal overflow, per the site's responsive baseline. - **Keyboard navigation**: Tab order on the gallery is top-to-bottom, one stop per card. Tab order on the detail page reaches the link rail before the MDX body. Focus indicators are visible in both themes (inherited from site-foundation's global focus styles).
